idea.description: SASRec predicts the next item by applying causal self-attention to a user's interaction history. Learned item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks with residual connections, normalization, and dropout. Candidate scores are dot products between sequence features and shared item embeddings. Training uses next-item supervision with sampled negatives. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781)
idea.motivation: Attention can select relevant recent actions while retaining access to longer histories, balancing the simplicity of Markov models with broader sequential context. The supplied idea establishes a baseline; it specifies no additional cold-start mechanism. My assessment is that users with no history and items without training interactions remain limitations.
idea.implementation_notes: Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and retain separate routing for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the environment's 200-epoch default. Preserve the provided splits and select using macro validation HR@10 under the pinned evaluator. Store artifacts beneath the trial directory and synchronize any architecture changes with the predictor writer. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), including measured metrics and definitions. Adapt probes to the actual trained module and available interaction/title/description/timestamp data. No experiments or benchmark results are reported here.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the fixed split using the baseline preprocessing.
  Initialize a category-specific SASRec model with training seed 42.
  For each training batch:
    Encode padded item sequences with positional embeddings and causal attention.
    Score shifted positive items and sampled negative items.
    Compute binary cross-entropy on nonpadding targets and update parameters.
  Save weights, configuration, and item mappings beneath the trial directory.
Write working/predict.py through the predictor writer, preserving category routing.
Use the host's fixed validation protocol to compare trials by macro HR@10.
Run compatible diagnostic probes and report only measured quantities.

originality.positive: The underlying paper introduced an influential application of self-attention to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: Score measures novelty relative to the required baseline: this proposal reuses SASRec without a specified new cold-start contribution.

future_potential.positive: Provides a foundation for testing regularization, sampling, and permitted metadata features within the shared search budget.
future_potential.negative: Any improvement requires validation; the supplied description provides no evidence of gains on these four categories.

code_difficulty.positive: On a 1–10 scale where higher means harder, baseline reuse limits implementation effort.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct masking, category mappings, predictor reconstruction, and diagnostic compatibility still require care.

report:
Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.
